newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-BULGARIA IGNORE STOICHKOV AGAINST LUXEMBOURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BULGARIA IGNORE STOICHKOV AGAINST LUXEMBOURG.

text.p: Bulgaria's volatile striker Hristo Stoichkov will not be involved in his country's World Cup qualifier against Luxembourg in June.

Stoichkov, who plays for Barcelona, is still at odds with Bulgarian Football Union chiefs for axing former national coach Dimitar Penev and dropping his nephew, Lyuboslav Penev, from the team for making insulting remarks on local television after Bulgaria's poor showing at Euro 96.
Stoichkov, who played a major role making Bulgaria a World Cup semifinalist for the first time in 1994, quit the national side last year after demanding the resignation of the soccer union chiefs.
But although he was named in Bulgaria's initial squad to face Cyprus in April, he declined to accept the invitation and coach Hristo Bonev has ignored him this time.
Ironically, though, striker Penev has been recalled along with Yordan Lechkov for the qualifier on June 8, which will be played in Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas.
Striker Radostin Kishishev, who has been named in all the World Cup qualifiers so far, has been left out.
In European group five Bulgaria lie second with nine points from four matches behind Israel who have 10 points from five matches.
